To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stress strain behavior of FRP confined concrete is significantly different from the behavior of concrete in circular columns, that the existing theoretical models are unable to provide satisfactory predictions, and that a design oriented stress strain models is presented that provides satisfactory predictions.

a simple design-oriented stress strain model can be developed for concrete confined with FRP in rectangular columns, which can be extended from an existing model developed for concrete confined by FRP in circular columns.
a new stress strain model for rectangular concrete confined with FRP was developed based on test results from both existing literature and a new set of tests conducted by the author.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a simple design oriented model for FRP confinement of rectangular columns.
the stress strain response of concrete in FRP-confined rectangular columns and the development of a design-oriented stress-strain model that can predict this behavior with reasonable accuracy.
the development of a stress strain model for concrete in FRP-confined rectangular columns that can be used to design such columns.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model is a good design oriented model for FRP-confined rectangular columns.
the proposed stress strain model provides satisfactory predictions of the behavior of FRP confined concrete rectangular columns.
the stress strain model proposed in this paper can provide satisfactory predictions of stress strain curves of FRP confined concrete for rectangular columns, which can be used for design purposes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the stress strain model presented in this paper can be used to estimate the stress strain behavior of concrete confined by rectangular FRP jackets, which is a key input to design of FRP jacketed concrete columns.
, the proposed stress strain model provides satisfactory predictions of the behavior of concrete in FRP-confined rectangular columns, and can be used in the design of such structures.
the existing models for rectangular columns are not satisfactory and a simple design-oriented model has to be developed for design purposes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the stress strain model developed by Wu et al. (2015, 2016) for FRP confined circular concrete can also be employed to predict the stress strain curves for FRP confined rectangular concrete with a good level of accuracy.

the design oriented stress strain curve for FRP confined circular concrete specimens can also be used to predict the stress strain curves of FRP confined concrete specimens in rectangular columns, provided the confinement is uniform and the concrete is confined by FRP in all directions.

the existing design oriented stress strain models for FRP confined circular concrete specimens, when extended to FRP confined rectangular concrete specimens, provide reasonable estimates of the stress strain behavior of the latter.
